_why: One job replaces the three Sunday Vercel crons that re-downloaded NY 2188, NJ 2250 and US 2199 unconditionally at 11:00, 11:20 and 11:40 UTC — and covers the other 49 jurisdictions those crons never touched. LegiScan rebuilds every session's bulk archive weekly but only a few actually change in a given week, so the sweep asks getSessionList and getDatasetList for every session's dataset_hash (two queries), compares them against the "LegiscanDatasets" ledger, and downloads only what moved. A full pass is 998 archives and roughly 30 GB; a steady-state Sunday is a few dozen megabytes. That is the difference between this and three crons that each pulled 20-70 MB every week whether or not a single bill had changed.
_ledger: "LegiscanDatasets" (state, session_id) -> dataset_hash is written by api/legiscan-sync.ts itself at the end of a SUCCESSFUL mode=dataset run, never before — so a dataset that failed is retried next week rather than recorded as done. A NULL hash means 'imported, hash unknown': the seed row this script writes once, from what "Bills" already holds, so the first weekly run does not re-download 650 archives to discover it already has them. Every import after the seed records its real hash, so the diff becomes exact from the second week on.
_state: The postal code for each session comes from getSessionList's own `state_abbr`, not from a table in the repo. api/legiscan-sync.ts's STATE_BY_ID had 31 as New Jersey; 31 is New Mexico and New Jersey is 30, which is how 28 New Mexico datasets were imported under ?state=NJ (their People and Roll Call rows still say NJ) and New Jersey's own nine bulk archives were never imported at all. A dataset whose state_id no list resolves is SKIPPED and named in the log, never imported under a guess — that guess is the entire bug.
_heap: heap_mb 4096 is on the driver, and the driver passes --heap 4096 to each run-handler child as well. The child is the one that needs it (NY's 2025-2026 archive is a 72 MB zip that is decompressed and mapped in memory); the parent's ceiling is there so that a future step added to this manifest inherits the same headroom rather than discovering it does not have it at 03:00.
_order: Sunday, weekday 0, and last of the five livingston manifests by filename — which is right: it is the only one that can run for hours, and run-due's MAX_CONCURRENT of 2 means a job launched ahead of it keeps its slot. A Sunday where it is deferred is due again on the next hourly catch-up, so the week is never skipped, only shifted.
